payload.comparison_population: postmortem MS cases with low levels of meningeal inflammation and GM demyelination
payload.symptoms: high levels of meningeal inflammation and GM demyelination
payload.supporting_quote: Increased expression of proinflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, TNF, IL2, and IL22) and molecules related to sustained B-cell activity and lymphoid-neogenesis (CXCL13, CXCL10, LTα, IL6, and IL10) was detected in the meninges and CSF of postmortem MS cases with high levels of meningeal inflammation and GM demyelination.

payload.comparison_population: MS patients with lower levels of GM damage at diagnosis
payload.symptoms: higher levels of GM damage at diagnosis
payload.supporting_quote: Similar proinflammatory patterns, including increased levels of CXCL13, TNF, IFNγ, CXCL12, IL6, IL8, and IL10, together with high levels of BAFF, APRIL, LIGHT, TWEAK, sTNFR1, sCD163, MMP2, and pentraxin III, were detected in the CSF of MS patients with higher levels of GM damage at diagnosis.

payload.comparison_population: patients with MS and pathologically confirmed leptomeningeal inflammation
payload.supporting_quote: Moreover, we observed high CXCL13:BAFF ratios in post mortem cerebral spinal fluid from patients with MS and pathologically confirmed leptomeningeal inflammation, as well as in living patients with MS and radiologically confirmed paramagnetic rim lesions.

payload.comparison_population: patients with MS and radiologically confirmed paramagnetic rim lesions
payload.supporting_quote: Moreover, we observed high CXCL13:BAFF ratios in post mortem cerebral spinal fluid from patients with MS and pathologically confirmed leptomeningeal inflammation, as well as in living patients with MS and radiologically confirmed paramagnetic rim lesions.
